items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: he composed a hit for us to do in the show which was 'Got to go tap dancing tonight,' which we still continue to convey

ctx.x: So, as a tap dancers got less and less, see, because now one of them had to go back to his school. He was a teacher. He had a school, and he had a student body. That was out white member was Jerry Ames. On -- see, because he took them out on tours, and they did some dances. You know, new dances, see, he was introducing. And he had to play these
commitments out. And so, that left us back on with -- we only had our composing tap dancer, John Rhythm Red. I called him (unintelligible). Debut John.

And he had a -- he composed a hit for us to do in the show which was "Got to go tap dancing tonight," which we still continue to convey, you see. And, see, he's not well now. And he's in intensive care, and we're trying to keep it going for his sake, and our choreographers' sake. Derby Wilson, he's away.
